classification.difficultyReason: Use the asymptote to determine the vertical shift, use the intercept to isolate the multiplier, then use the negative-input point to determine the base before evaluating the function at −3.

content.prompt: The point $(-3,p)$ lies on the graph of the exponential function $y=k\times a^x+c$, shown in the diagram below. The points $\left(-1,-\frac12\right)$ and $(0,-1)$ also lie on the same graph.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 16 graph between the stem and parts (a) and (b), printed page 238
spec.description: A decreasing blue exponential curve with arrows at both ends, positive-direction axis arrows, three marked points and a dashed horizontal asymptote. The source has no axis ticks or grid. House styling uses black for ordinary axes, labels, guide and point markers.
spec.mathematics: The curve is plotted from the unique exponential determined by the two given coordinates and the asymptote. It passes through the point labelled (-3,p), crosses the x-axis between x=-3 and x=-1, and approaches y=-2 from above.
spec.answerVisibility: The curve label is y=k×a^x+c and the unknown ordinate is labelled p. The student diagram displays no solved parameter values, numerical value of p or intercept coordinates beyond the supplied point labels.

answer.worked:
The horizontal asymptote is $y=-2$, so $c=-2$. Substitute $(0,-1)$.
$$\begin{align*}-1&=k\cdot a^0-2\\-1&=k-2\\k&=1.\end{align*}$$
Substitute $\left(-1,-\frac12\right)$.
$$\begin{align*}-\frac12&=a^{-1}-2\\\frac32&=\frac1a\\a&=\frac23.\end{align*}$$
